subject: general
question:
Who said the following words?

"The United Nations was not created to take humanity to heaven, but to save it from hell."
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dag Hammarskjold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dag Hammarskjold** was the second Secretary-General of the United Nations, serving from April 1953 until his death in a plane crash in September 1961.
 
• Hammarskjold is widely regarded as one of the most effective UN Secretaries-General due to his active role in diplomacy and peacekeeping missions.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize posthumously in 1961 for his efforts to strengthen the United Nations and promote peace.
 
• Hammarskjold's tenure was marked by his dedication to international cooperation and his belief in the UN's mission to prevent conflict and protect humanity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Nations (UN)**

 
 
• The United Nations is an international organization founded in 1945 after the Second World War by 51 countries committed to maintaining international peace and security, developing friendly relations among nations, and promoting social progress, better living standards, and human rights.
 
• The UN's mission and work are guided by the purposes and principles contained in its founding Charter, which was signed in San Francisco on June 26, 1945.
 
• The organization now has 193 member states and works on a vast array of issues, including peace and security, climate change, sustainable development, human rights, disarmament, terrorism, humanitarian and health emergencies, gender equality, governance, and international law.
 
• The principal organs of the UN include the General Assembly, the Security Council, the Economic and Social Council, the International Court of Justice, and the UN Secretariat.
 
 
 
• **Secretary-General of the United Nations**
 
 
• The Secretary-General is the head of the United Nations Secretariat, one of the principal organs of the UN, and acts as the de facto spokesperson and leader of the organization.
 
• The Secretary-General is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council, typically for a five-year term, which can be renewed.
 
• The role involves providing administrative guidance to the UN, mediating international disputes, and implementing the decisions of the UN's principal organs.
 
• Notable Secretaries-General include Trygve Lie (the first Secretary-General), Dag Hammarskjold, U Thant, Kurt Waldheim, Javier Pérez de Cuéllar, Boutros Boutros-Ghali, Kofi Annan, Ban Ki-moon, and the current Secretary-General António Guterres.
